biodiversity_overview.text: 1,556 GBIF occurrence records for 27 tracked species are attributed to Chandigarh, spanning 1982-2026.
1,539 of these records (98.9%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 16, Magnoliopsida 5, Mammalia 4, Testudines 2.

threatened_species.text: 3 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Grey-Hornbill (540), Indian Spot-billed Duck (263), Common Peafowl (159), Indian White-eye (126), Indian Pond-heron (60).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 147 in 2016 to 21 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 0.42% of Chandigarh's area (2 areas intersect the state).
0.0% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (0 of 1,539); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Small Indian Mongoose (0.47), Indian Ash Tree (0.36), Indian Roofed Turtle (0.36), Indian Gooseberry (0.35), Bulletwood (0.30).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 6 km2 (5.66% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

0.1 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (0.89% of the 2000 extent; 0.0% in 2015-2024, rank 33 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2006 (0.03 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 18.37% of land and population density is 6,951.1 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
54% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.
